fields.h1: Build a Sponsorship Form That Sells Tiers and Sorts Requests
fields.hero_description: Create a sponsorship form that closes tiers as they sell out and collects a print-ready logo from every sponsor.
fields.features_heading: What a Sponsorship Form Should Handle
fields.features_subheading: A PDF records a pledge. These six pieces turn it into a sponsor with artwork on file and an invoice on the way.
fields.feature_1:
Tiers that close when they sell out

Set a price and a slot count for each tier. Every signed sponsor uses up one slot, and the tier leaves the form when the last one goes. Sponsors see what is left as they choose.
fields.feature_2:
Logo uploads checked on arrival

Ask for artwork in the format your printer needs, such as SVG or EPS. A sponsor who uploads a blurry JPG sees the problem before leaving the page, not after the proof comes back.
fields.feature_3:
Requests sorted by the amount asked

Companies that receive pitches can route each one by size. Small asks go to one person to decide, while larger ones queue for a committee with the event date and audience attached.
fields.feature_4:
An agreement signed at submit

Show the benefits of the chosen tier and the cancellation terms, then collect a signature. The signed record stays on the sponsor's row for whoever orders the banners and signs.
fields.feature_5:
Draft invoices in your accounting tool

Connect QuickBooks or Xero and each confirmed sponsor becomes a draft invoice with its tier and amount. Your treasurer reviews and sends it, and nobody retypes a pledge from paper.
fields.feature_6:
Export the code when you outgrow it

On paid plans, move the full codebase to your GitHub repository once the form grows into a member portal or an event app. Host it wherever you like and keep building on it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Groups That Run Sponsorships Online
fields.tab_content_1:
Lunch closes itself after the third sponsor

Every spring the Greenfield Chamber of Commerce sells sponsorships for its golf outing on one form: 18 hole signs at $500 or 3 lunch slots at $1,000. Each sponsor uploads a logo for the sign. When the third lunch sponsor signs, the lunch tier drops off the form and the treasurer gets a draft invoice in QuickBooks.
fields.tab_content_2:
No jersey goes to print without a logo

Jersey printers want artwork weeks before opening day. Riverside Youth Soccer needs a print-ready logo from each team sponsor by February 15. The coordinator sees which of the 12 sponsored teams are still missing art, and each late sponsor gets an email reminder every 3 days.
fields.tab_content_3:
Anything over $2,500 waits for the committee

Lakeshore Credit Union gets dozens of sponsorship asks a month from schools and local leagues. Requests up to $2,500 go to Dana, the community manager, to decide. When the Westfield High robotics team asked for $4,000, the request went on the giving committee's agenda for its monthly meeting.
fields.tab_content_4:
With $87,000 committed, only Gold has room left

Six weeks out from the Harborview Product Summit, Platinum and Silver have sold out and $87,000 is committed. Two of the 6 Gold packages are still unsold at $7,500 each. The events lead pulls last year's sponsors who skipped Gold and emails them the floor plan with the open booths marked.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Sponsorship Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a sponsorship form that prices each tier and collects every logo, then build and test it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick which side of the deal you are on
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Price each tier and cap its slots
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for the artwork you will print
fields.howto_step_1_des: A sponsorship form either sells packages to sponsors or takes requests from groups asking for support. Organizers need tiers and an agreement. Companies on the receiving end need the event details and the amount requested, plus a fair way to compare asks.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Price each tier before you write a single question, and set how many slots it has. List what a sponsor gets at each level, such as a hole sign or a booth. The form shows those benefits next to the price.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Name the file types and the deadline your printer or venue gives you. Ask for the logo and the company name exactly as it should appear, plus a contact for artwork questions. A missing file then surfaces weeks before the print run.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose who decides on incoming requests and how quickly. A small ask can go to one manager, while anything above your threshold waits for the committee. Name a backup for the weeks that person is away, and write the reply a declined group receives.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your tiers and routing rules into one prompt. Emergent builds the form with a sponsors table behind it, plus a dashboard of pledges by tier. Change a tier price or a deadline later by asking for it in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect the tools that follow up
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect QuickBooks or Xero for invoices, and Slack or email for alerts. The events lead hears about each new pledge without opening the dashboard. Requests over your threshold post to the committee's channel instead of a shared inbox.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run a test sponsor through the whole form before the link goes out. Pick the smallest tier and upload a JPG to check the file rule. Sign the agreement, then confirm that the draft invoice and the alert both arrived.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Sponsorship Form That Sells Tiers and Sorts Requests' covers both sides (selling and receiving); title 'Free Sponsorship Form Builder | Emergent'; hero 'Create a sponsorship form that closes tiers as they sell out and collects a print-ready logo from every sponsor.' is under 130 characters; how-to description is one sentence under 140.

intent.evidence: Builder-fit SERP served: working builder with tiers, logos, routing; example (FAQ 3), templates (FAQ 9), free (FAQ 7), PDF vs online (FAQ 5), request form contents (FAQ 10), seven-step how-to.

specificity.evidence: Sponsorship vocabulary: '18 hole signs at $500 or 3 lunch slots at $1,000', 'print-ready logo', 'giving committee', 'Platinum and Silver have sold out', 'in-kind section'.

openers.evidence: Feature bodies open on verbs ('Set a price and a slot count', 'Ask for artwork', 'Show the benefits', 'Connect QuickBooks or Xero'); tabs open on full sentences ('Every spring the Greenfield Chamber of Commerce sells sponsorships').

craft.evidence: One idea per sentence, e.g. 'Sponsors see what is left as they choose.' No blocking craft defect.

voice.evidence: Concrete operator detail: 'A sponsor who uploads a blurry JPG sees the problem before leaving the page, not after the proof comes back.' Cross-page formula logged as a note.

truth.evidence: In-kind definition sourced (sponsorshipcollective); tab 4 sums hold (2 x $15,000 + 4 x $7,500 + 9 x $3,000 = $87,000; 2 of 6 Gold left; 15 of 17); 7 + 11 = 18 hole signs; 9 + 3 = 12 teams; e-signature claim stays within e-signature-capture (no legal validity claim).

distinct.evidence: Golf outing, youth league jerseys, credit union giving and conference packages are unique to this page; no proposal or RFP sibling primary in a heading; creator pitches handed to the creator application link.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, answer-first, no brand or file-format ask in a question, hub link in item 2, exact-match links to registration form and creator application, moat lines in items 7 and 9, all seven secondaries carried.

images.evidence: Contact sheet matches copy: 'Lunch tier sold out, 3 of 3 slots taken', 'Hole signs: 18 at $500, 7 sold, 11 left', '12 sponsored teams, 9 logos in, 3 missing', 'Next reminder in 3 days', 'Westfield robotics, $4,000', '$87,000 committed', '2 of 6 Gold left'.
